description: Verify that the time interval between consecutive ARP Announcements is in [ANNOUNCE_INTERVAL - 50 ms, ANNOUNCE_INTERVAL + 50 ms] (RFC 3927 §2.4, MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
RFC 3927 §2.4 sets ANNOUNCE_INTERVAL = 2 s between consecutive Announcements. The harness allows ±50 ms tolerance to absorb scheduler jitter. Wrong cadence means either Announcements arrive too close together (less robust to loss) or too far apart (cache update is delayed).

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: OpStartLLAutoconf (kicks the Link-Local state machine; cadence-verification cases use the spec-default rates rather than the fast envelope)

2. DUT: 3 Probes → 2 Announcements.

3. Observation:
   • Δt(announce[1] - announce[0]) ∈ [ANNOUNCE_INTERVAL - 50 ms, ANNOUNCE_INTERVAL + 50 ms]   ← key check

[Pass condition]
Both Announcements emitted AND inter-Announcement Δt is inside the bound.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_announces — DUT did not emit any Announcement after the Probe phase
• Fail_only_one_announce — fewer than 2 Announcements within the deadline
• Fail_interval_out_of_range — inter-Announcement interval is outside the RFC 3927 bounds (with 50 ms tolerance)

verdicts.Pass: Announcement interval is inside [ANNOUNCE_INTERVAL ± 50 ms] — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_announces: DUT did not emit any ARP Announcement after Probes
verdicts.Fail_only_one_announce: Fewer than 2 ARP Announcements within the deadline
verdicts.Fail_interval_out_of_range: Announcement interval is outside the RFC 3927 bounds (50 ms tolerance)
